arguments.reason: This lens compares the NL contract set against the exact source inventory and closed FCSTM topology to find structural/containment/endpoint/owner-entry defects. Key findings: (1) Root/system initial entry to Operate is satisfied (OffState->OperateState via 'start', and [*]->OffState exists), but the Operate-local composite regions (IdleRegion/AccelerateRegion/BrakeRegion) each nest a leaf state (IdleState/AcceleratingState/BrakingState) that has NO exact initial pseudostate edge targeting it - each region's [*] targets only the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state, leaving the authored substates IdleState/AcceleratingState/BrakingState permanently unreachable from initial. This is a distinct default-entry defect per region-owned substate. (2) The NL3 substate transitions (Idle->Accelerating, Accelerating->Braking, Braking->Idle, Cruising->Braking) are modeled only at the region level (IdleRegion->AccelerateRegion, etc.), and the named leaf states IdleState/AcceleratingState/BrakingState that the endpoint contracts reference are unreachable, so the literal named-state endpoints are not realized by any reachable transition - only region-level surrogates exist. (3) Cardinality: Operate composite direct children are the three regions (IdleRegion/AccelerateRegion/BrakeRegion), not the four named states, which bears on the cardinality binding.

arguments.reason: This lens audits root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, and dead-end/frontier facts for the power-on/power-off, Operate-local containment, and transition-endpoint contracts against the closed FCSTM. The model uses three orthogonal-looking regions (IdleRegion, AccelerateRegion, BrakeRegion) each with a leaf named state (IdleState/AcceleratingState/BrakingState) and a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state; the leaf named states are unreachable from the machine's initial entry because each region's own initial pseudostate targets only UnspecifiedInitial, not the named leaf. This produces reachable-consumer gaps for Accelerate/Brake/Reach_Speed/Stop-triggered transitions that are declared on the named leaf states (IdleState, AcceleratingState, BrakingState) since their only reachable consumers are the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial siblings, not the named substates referenced by NL3's substate transition contracts. I derive one event_consumer_coverage-style unreachable-operating-state defect against the exact NL3 endpoint contracts because the concrete named source states (Idle/Accelerating/Braking) required as sources of the Operate-local transitions are unreachable, making the specific accelerating/braking/stopping-triggered transition obligations effectively unreachable/dead consumer paths even though same-effect transitions exist from the synthetic sibling. I also verified NL1/NL2 root power-on/off endpoints and NL1 initial-entry are satisfied (OffState->OperateState via start; OperateState->OffState guarded R45RouteToken==10 realizing keyOff; root [*]->OffState satisfies NL1's power-on initial entry through Off then start-triggered entry into Operate). Termination is not applicable here since Off/root is not stated as a completion state distinct from the operate/off cycle.

This is corroborated by deterministic STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL diagnostics and verify_facts reachability refutations, and by explicit S2 backend receipts (verdict=false) for the three owner-local initial-entry obligations that were predicate-bound (i8, i9, i10) and the root-to-Operate initial entry (i15, itself unresolved due to frontier binding_status=identity_unresolved despite a receipt existing). The transition_endpoint obligations (i1..i6) consistently show that region-to-region surrogate edges exist but the exact named leaf source/target states are unreachable, which is a distinct but consistent transition_endpoints defect; the strongest rebuttal (region-level edges count as satisfying the named-leaf contract) is a competent alternative reading against an exact-named-substate contract, since PlantUML source itself declares transitions at region granularity in some cases, making this a genuine undercutting alternative rather than a clearly defeated one — however the dossiers also supply explicit reachable_consumer_state_refs exclusion facts (event-consumer analysis) showing the named leaf is never a reachable consumer, which more strongly establishes the violation while leaving the region-level-proxy reading as a surviving undercutting alternative (D1) rather than fully defeating it, since no exact contract text forecloses the coarser region-level reading. The pure containment obligations (i0) admit a technically-satisfied nesting relation but effectively-unreachable operative substate; treated as established with a surviving rebutting reading that containment (nesting) itself holds, distinct from reachability. The frontier-unresolved containment/cardinality/init obligations lacking any element_refs (i11-i14, i16) and the root initial-entry frontier obligation i15 have binding_status=identity_unresolved with no reproducible model reference, so despite an S2 receipt attached to i15's plan, the candidate's own binding record indicates the frontier check remains genuinely unresolved as supplied; these are marked grounding=unresolved. i7's G1 plan is unsupported (predicate outside executable fragment) but exact reachability diagnostics/verify_facts already establish the named-substate unreachability independently, so grounding=established despite predicate-null.</parameter>

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL (IdleState:line:11, AcceleratingState:line:23, BrakingState:line:39); verify_facts.non_proved reachability refutations for the same three states; inspection_equivalent_facts.states reachable_from_initial=false for these refs; inspection_equivalent_facts transitions line:13/25/26/41 ([*] -> UnspecifiedInitial in each region) reachable_from_initial=false/true showing the initial pseudostate never targets the named leaf.
issues.expected: The three named Operate-local substates (Idle, Accelerating, Braking) required by NL3 as behaviorally meaningful loci must be reachable from the machine's root initial entry so the accelerating/braking/stopping-driven transitions can actually occur from them.
issues.observed: Deterministic reachability facts (inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics + verify_facts refuted checks) show IdleState:line:11, AcceleratingState:line:23, and BrakingState:line:39 are all not reachable from the top-level initial entry in the finite hierarchy; each region's own initial pseudostate targets only its synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state instead.
issues.reason: This is a distinct reachability property from the individual transition_endpoints contracts: even if a region-to-region edge with the correct event exists, the exact named substate that NL3 designates as the operational locus is never entered, which is a root/region-level reachability defect independent of any single transition's existence.

issues.strongest_rebuttal: The composite regions themselves (IdleRegion, AccelerateRegion, BrakeRegion) are reachable and their synthetic UnspecifiedInitial substates provide operationally equivalent Accelerate/Brake/Reach_Speed/Stop/keyOff consumers with identical effects, so the named leaf states might be considered cosmetic decorations of an otherwise-working region-level state machine rather than a genuine behavioral gap.
issues.title: Named Operate-local substates Idle, Accelerating, and Braking are unreachable from the top-level initial entry

The closed FCSTM realizes each region's initial pseudostate edge only into a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state, leaving the actually-named leaf states (IdleState, AcceleratingState, BrakingState) permanently unreachable from the top-level initial entry, per deterministic diagnostics and verify facts. This is a distinct reachability property from the NL3 transition_endpoints contracts, which only require the existence of an edge between two named concepts and do not by themselves establish that the named source state is reachable.
additional_contracts.scope: Operate-local named substates required by NL3 substate transitions

cardinality_bindings.alternative_reading: An alternative reading treats OperateState's direct children as concurrent_regions (IdleRegion, AccelerateRegion, BrakeRegion) since the PlantUML source groups the four named substates into three region composites with no explicit UML region separator; under this reading the counted member_domain would be concurrent_regions or direct_child_states of the regions themselves rather than of OperateState, and the four named substates would only be reachable as an explicit_named_members set two levels below Operate. This remains a materially different, also-competent domain choice for the deterministic frontier and D-level review.
cardinality_bindings.basis: NL-CONTRACT-NL1-DERIVED-43caece8ab325d2d2190 quote 'it transitions between Idle, Accelerating or Cruising, and Braking states'; exact_source_inventory.states OperateState (source_id=OperateState); closed_model_inventory/inspection_equivalent_facts state:OperateState:line:9 with children IdleRegion/AccelerateRegion/BrakeRegion; deeper nesting shows Idle/Accelerating/Cruising/Braking as grandchildren via IdleRegion/AccelerateRegion/BrakeRegion.
cardinality_bindings.reason: NL1 explicitly enumerates the finite set of substates (Idle, Accelerating or Cruising, Braking) transitioned between within the Operate composite, establishing a direct child-state cardinality obligation on the Operate owner. In the closed model, OperateState directly contains three composite regions (IdleRegion, AccelerateRegion, BrakeRegion) rather than four leaf states directly; the four named substates are each nested one level deeper inside these regions. This lens's primary reading follows the NL's plain scope_concept (Operate) and member_concept (named substates: Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, Braking) as the counted direct children of Operate, consistent with the contract's explicit scope_concept='Operate composite substate membership' and required_count=4.

branches.reason: This lens audits root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, and dead-end/frontier facts for the power-on/power-off, Operate-local containment, and transition-endpoint contracts against the closed FCSTM. The model uses three orthogonal-looking regions (IdleRegion, AccelerateRegion, BrakeRegion) each with a leaf named state (IdleState/AcceleratingState/BrakingState) and a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state; the leaf named states are unreachable from the machine's initial entry because each region's own initial pseudostate targets only UnspecifiedInitial, not the named leaf. This produces reachable-consumer gaps for Accelerate/Brake/Reach_Speed/Stop-triggered transitions that are declared on the named leaf states (IdleState, AcceleratingState, BrakingState) since their only reachable consumers are the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial siblings, not the named substates referenced by NL3's substate transition contracts. I derive one event_consumer_coverage-style unreachable-operating-state defect against the exact NL3 endpoint contracts because the concrete named source states (Idle/Accelerating/Braking) required as sources of the Operate-local transitions are unreachable, making the specific accelerating/braking/stopping-triggered transition obligations effectively unreachable/dead consumer paths even though same-effect transitions exist from the synthetic sibling. I also verified NL1/NL2 root power-on/off endpoints and NL1 initial-entry are satisfied (OffState->OperateState via start; OperateState->OffState guarded R45RouteToken==10 realizing keyOff; root [*]->OffState satisfies NL1's power-on initial entry through Off then start-triggered entry into Operate). Termination is not applicable here since Off/root is not stated as a completion state distinct from the operate/off cycle.
